items.t: UBS Landlord Puts Zurich Campus on the Block as Vontobel Lifts Target to CHF 42.50
sum: Norway's sovereign wealth fund is looking to offload the Üetlihof in Zurich before the year is out, a sale that would change hands on a property UBS occupies as tenant rather than owns. The bank's lease at the site runs until 2037, according to AWP, while both the buyer and the price remain undecided. UBS told the NZZ that the Üetlihof is an important location for the bank — a signal that the tenancy, not the title, is what matters to the lender.

The disposal talk surfaced alongside a busier flow of corporate news from the Swiss giant. Vontobel on Thursday raised its price target on UBS from CHF 40 to CHF 42.50, though the research house kept its rating at "Hold" and pointedly declined to attach a buy call to the higher number. UBS shares finished Friday at EUR 43.83.

On the regulatory front, a possible compromise is taking shape. According to Bloomberg, a proposal aired on 4 November by a member of Switzerland's National Council would permit a different valuation method for foreign subsidiaries. The scope of the plan and the political backing behind it were still unclear, the report said. The National Council's economic and tax commission had planned to continue detailed deliberations on UBS's capital adequacy at its meeting on 23 and 24 November.

Media reports suggest the proposal from parliament's larger chamber would let UBS apply more conservative valuation methods when calculating the extra capital required for its overseas units. That could shrink the additional USD 16bn the bank expects to need, though the outcome and the size of any relief remain open.

For the third quarter of 2026, UBS reported on 28 October a net profit of USD 2.7bn. Return on CET1 capital came in at 14.8%, according to company figures. By the end of 2026, UBS expects its CET1 ratio to land near its target of roughly 14%. Moody's confirmed the bank's ratings on 3 November.

On the funding side, UBS AG said on Thursday it will redeem all outstanding securities across ten ETRACS ETN series, with settlement scheduled for 17 and 18 December. For BDCZ, the formal notice of termination is not due until 24 November, meaning that series still awaits its announced notification ahead of the planned wind-down.

AMD Stock Surges as UBS Reports 31% Jump in Server CPU Shipments
sum: - UBS reported a 31% year-over-year increase in global server CPU shipments in Q3 2026
- UBS projected that the CPU market could reach approximately $210 billion by 2030

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) received another boost on Nov. 11, after a new UBS report revealed that global server CPU shipments surged 31% year over year in the third quarter of 2026. The findings revealed growing demand for data center processors, which strengthened the outlook for AMD.
AMD shares rallied during Wednesday's session, supported by the encouraging UBS findings and strong earnings from AI cloud computing company CoreWeave.

According to UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri, global server CPU shipments increased approximately 31% compared to the previous year and 6% from the preceding quarter. The quarterly growth exceeded the typical seasonal increase of around 3%.

AMD maintained approximately 28.4% of the server CPU market by unit shipments, while rival Intel saw its share decline by 2.4 percentage points to 51.5%. Meanwhile, Arm-based processors gained 2.5 percentage points, reaching 20.1%.
Although AMD's market share stayed relatively stable, the rapid expansion of the overall market suggests the company is benefiting from increased demand for its EPYC server processors.

Kalyan Jewellers shares surge 10% as Q2 profit jumps 64%; UBS sees big upside, check target price
sum: Kalyan Jewellers share price: Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India surged 10 percent to Rs 672 in early trade on Wednesday, after the jewellery retailer reported a 64 percent year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit for the fiscal second quarter, supported by strong revenue growth. Brokerage firm UBS maintained its Buy rating on the stock, with a target price of Rs 900, implying an upside of around 47 percent from Monday's closing price.

The sharp rally followed Kalyan Jewellers' Q2 FY27 results, which showed consolidated revenue crossing the Rs 10,000-crore mark, while the company's management expressed optimism about jewellery demand during the ongoing festive and wedding season.

Kalyan Jewellers shares have gained 38.4 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined around 3 percent during the same period. At the current market price, the company commands a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 69,000 crore.

Kalyan Jewellers reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 427 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, up 63.6 percent from Rs 260.51 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 73 crore from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding this gain, net profit stood at approximately Rs 354 crore, representing an increase of nearly 36 percent year-on-year.

Revenue from operations climbed 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 7,856 crore in the year-ago period, reflecting strong growth in the company's jewellery retail business.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 29.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 644.7 crore. However, the EBITDA margin edged lower to 6.25 percent from 6.33 percent a year earlier, indicating broadly stable operating profitability despite the strong revenue expansion.

For the first half of FY27, Kalyan Jewellers reported a 48 percent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 776 crore, compared with Rs 525 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue for the six-month period rose 38 percent to Rs 20,912 crore from Rs 15,125 crore in the first half of FY26.

Andritz stock: UBS conference follows record backlog
sum: ANDRITZ is scheduled to take part in the UBS European Conference in London on Tuesday, November 10, and Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The company lists the investor conference in its official financial calendar.

The event follows ANDRITZ's third-quarter report published on October 29. In that release, the group said its order backlog reached EUR 12,729.1 million as of September 30, a record high and 21.7% above the level at the end of 2025. The backlog gives investors a current measure of the revenue base supporting future project execution.

ANDRITZ reported third-quarter revenue of EUR 2,059.6 million, up 9.2% from the year-earlier quarter. Comparable EBITA increased to EUR 184.9 million, while the comparable EBITA margin was 9.0%, compared with 8.9% a year earlier.

For the first nine months, revenue reached EUR 5,900.9 million, an increase of 6.5%. Order intake totaled EUR 8,085.9 million, up 17.1% year on year, with Hydropower and Metals providing the strongest growth contributions. These figures come from the company's Q3 2026 results release.

Management confirmed its full-year 2026 guidance. ANDRITZ continues to expect revenue between EUR 8.0 billion and EUR 8.3 billion and a comparable EBITA margin between 8.7% and 9.1%. The conference therefore gives investors a scheduled opportunity to assess how the group frames execution, demand and the conversion of its backlog after the latest quarterly figures.
Andritz stock traded at EUR 81.40 on Lang & Schwarz at 17:40 CET on Sunday, November 8, 2026; the real-time quote of Andritz stock is available here.

sum: UBS raised its target on Lenskart to Rs 850 from Rs 800 earlier, calling it one of the most compelling compounding stories in India's consumer sector.

Lenskart Solutions Ltd shares rallied 11 per cent in Thursday's trade amid sharp upward revisions in target prices by a handful of domestic and foreign brokerages. These included UBS, which raised its target on Lenskart to Rs 850 from Rs 800 earlier, calling it one of the most compelling compounding stories in India's consumer sector. Morgan Stanley raised its target to Rs 805 from Rs 718.

ICICI Securities now values the stock at Rs 800, up from Rs 700 earlier. Goldman Sachs raised its target to Rs 800 from Rs 715, Emkay to Rs 800 from Rs 775, CLSA to Rs 773 from Rs 743 and Antique Stock Broking to Rs 660 from Rs 600.
On Wednesday, the scrip rose 11.05 per cent to hit a high of Rs 767.40 apiece.

Analysts said Lenskart has built strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category through a centralised, automated manufacturing facility and logistics network, strong backward integration and a large omnichannel presence.

HSBC upgraded the stock to 'Buy' and raised its target price to Rs 790 on higher estimates and a higher valuation multiple for its international business. Following the Q2 results, the foreign brokerage said its key upgrades were in India Ebitda margins, where the pace of expansion was higher, leading to an 8 per cent increase in its FY28 Ebitda estimates. For the international business, HSBC assumed higher growth and greater margin improvement.

"Our store expansion is higher than management estimates as we expect a pick-up. This drives a 17 per cent increase in international FY28e EBITDA. We roll forward our valuation to December 2027 and increase the international business target EV/EBITDA to 40x, from 30x, reflecting greater confidence in its growth and margin, while retaining 45x for India," it said.

Dangote Cement stock: Goldman, UBS join London listing plans
sum: Dangote Cement stock is gaining attention after Goldman Sachs and UBS joined preparations for a possible London Stock Exchange listing. BusinessDay reported on October 15, 2026 that the company could pursue the transaction as early as November, with a proposed secondary sale targeting up to 1 billion US dollars.

The reported transaction would involve existing shareholders selling part of their holdings rather than Dangote Cement issuing new shares. Goldman Sachs and UBS would join other banks working on the proposed offering, which is intended to give the company access to a broader international investor base.

The London plan would complement Dangote Cement's existing listing on the Nigerian Exchange. For investors, a second listing could create an additional venue for trading and establish a reference point for the company's valuation among international institutions. The proposal does not by itself confirm that a transaction will be completed.

BusinessDay said the listing could take place as early as November. The timetable remains dependent on regulatory approvals, final terms and market conditions, while the reported sale structure would direct proceeds to selling shareholders rather than directly to Dangote Cement.

Investors should therefore distinguish between progress in arranging the transaction and a completed London debut. The appointment of bookrunners can advance preparation, but it does not establish the final offer size, pricing or admission date.

Dangote Cement Plc produces and sells cement across Sub-Saharan Africa, with operations in ten countries and production capacity of 55.0 million tonnes per year, according to the company website. Its strategy focuses on serving construction demand in West and Central Africa and using Nigeria as an export hub. The group competes with regional cement producers including BUA Cement and Lafarge Africa in Nigeria, while its broad African footprint gives it a larger geographic reach than more locally focused rivals.
Broader market conditions remain relevant for companies seeking international listings. Current market reports provide the wider market context.

sum: Shares of Jabil Inc. (JBL) jumped nearly 6% on Tuesday after UBS upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral,’ as the firm sees Big Tech’s AI investments providing a boost to the company in the coming years.
By midday Tuesday, JBL stock had pared some of its gains but was still trading 4.3% higher.
UBS analyst David Vogt upgraded Jabil to ‘Buy’ while keeping the price target unchanged at $430, implying nearly 28% upside from Monday’s close.

The firm said “product road maps” from key customers, including Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Meta Platforms Inc. (META), and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), could mean potentially faster growth than previously expected.

“We upgrade Jabil to Buy on a multi-year growth cycle fueled by AI investment from Amazon, Meta, and Google,” the analyst wrote, according to a report in Barron’s. UBS added that rising health care demand and “scaling automation and robotics markets” will also be tailwinds for the company.
The firm forecasts Jabil’s AI-related revenue growing by about 50% to $20.3 billion in fiscal 2027, up from $13.5 billion in fiscal 2026.

Amazon is the key for Jabil, according to UBS, the Barron’s report stated. “Amazon, Jabil’s largest AI partner, plans to accelerate deployment of its Graviton CPUs and Trainium AI ASICs over the next several years,” the analyst wrote.

UBS Flags a Bullish Setup in Tesla Stock and Lifts Its Price Target
sum: UBS just raised its Tesla price target and called the risk/reward tactically favorable, but the same stock lost 32% in 30 days after one bad earnings report. Here is what the bull case actually rests on.

UBS analyst Joseph Spak raised his price target on Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA | TSLA Price Prediction) to $391, according to UBS from $385, according to UBS and kept his Buy rating. The argument behind the modest bump carries the weight. Tesla shares trade at $378.02, down 16.6% over the past year and 15.94% year to date. They are also up 7.14% over the past week and 6.76% over the past month. Spak is making a tactical call on a stock that has started moving again after a weak year.

Spak’s core claim is direct: “Tesla remains more sentiment- than results-driven, and at current levels, the risk/reward looks tactically favorable.” Put simply, the share price moves on what investors expect from robotaxis, robots and AI. Quarterly profits play a smaller role.

The record supports him. In Q2 2026, Tesla earned $0.33 per share, missing the $0.5367 estimate. The stock fell 14.52% on the day of the report, then gained 9.15% over the next 30 days. The S&P 500 ETF rose 3.43% over the same period. At roughly 396x earnings, the price rests on expectations about the future: Robotaxi service in seven U.S. metros and 1.48M active FSD subscriptions. Investors who value Tesla on fundamentals will find current profits explain little of the stock’s behavior.

The call is about near-term positioning. Spak’s move from $385 to $391 tells you the underlying model barely changed. Spak’s message is that conditions currently favor the bulls. Third-quarter deliveries came in ahead of consensus estimates, and options traders lean bullish, with a full-chain put/call ratio of 0.59. That means call contracts outnumber puts.

A stock that rises on mood can fall on mood too, even when the business hasn’t changed. Today Tesla is down 0.7% in premarket trading after European self-driving approvals were delayed. After the Q4 2024 report, shares lost 32.04% over 30 days.

The fundamentals give little support if the mood turns. Operating margin fell to 1.4% in Q2. Free cash flow came in at -$1.09B, and management expects 2026 capex above $25 billion. Automotive margins excluding credits slipped from 19.2% to 16.3%.

sum: IG Group Holdings Plc (LSE:IGG), the online trading platform, suffered a 22% share-price fall last Friday (Oct. 2) after cutting its 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance, but UBS described the sell-off as an overreaction.
The bank's analyst Haley Tam and colleagues cut their earnings-per-share forecasts by 13% for 2026 through 2028 and reduced the price target to 1,425p from 1,700p, while retaining a 'buy' rating.

UBS said IG's weaker third-quarter performance reflected lower over-the-counter, or OTC, revenue retention, which fell to about 70% from an average of about 80% since market-making optimisation measures were introduced in the second half of 2025.
The broker said those measures had improved average retention from about 75% historically to 80% but created greater short-term volatility that contributed to the latest decline.
IG now expects 2026 revenue growth in the mid-single-digit percentage range and an EBITDA margin in the low 40s, below the stronger outlook issued earlier this year.

UBS said the bigger issue for investors was not simply the earnings miss but the damage to confidence after IG cut guidance only four months after raising it, following the cancellation of buybacks and a larger-than-expected acquisition.

The broker believes the market has treated the Q3 weakness as a permanent deterioration when it is more likely to be a one-off setback, although it now forecasts only 7% organic revenue growth annually between 2025 and 2030.

UBS reiterated its buy rating on Bloom Energy (BE) stock this week, even as shares have pulled back more than 20% since late June.

The concern weighing on Bloom Energy stock centers on raw materials, specifically the risk that scandium, a rare element used in Bloom’s fuel cell technology, could become a bottleneck for the company’s growth.

UBS analyst Manav Gupta directly pushed back on that concern. In a Thursday note to clients, he said the recent pullback actually creates an attractive buying opportunity, arguing that fears around raw material sourcing, and scandium specifically, are overstated.

Gupta pointed out that Bloom has developed its own proprietary process to secure the scandium it needs, which helps insulate the company from broader supply constraints that might affect competitors relying on more traditional sourcing methods.

items.t: UBS Faces Challenges Revamping U.S. Wealth Management Amid Asset Outflows and Adviser Departures
sum: UBS Group is encountering significant hurdles in its efforts to turnaround its U.S. wealth management business after experiencing substantial client asset outflows and the loss of nearly 200 financial advisers over the past year.
The bank reported a net asset outflow of USD14.1 billion in the Americas during Q4 2025, resulting in a net annual outflow of USD6 billion.

These outflows and adviser departures, driven by factors such as higher compensation and better growth opportunities at rival firms, have complicated UBS’s goal of expanding and improving profitability in the critical U.S. market. Competitors including Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Charles Schwab, and RBC have successfully recruited former UBS advisers, further intensifying the challenge.

UBS aims to increase its U.S. wealth management pre-tax margin to 15 percent this year, up from 13 percent in 2025, but still well below margins in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. CEO Sergio Ermotti has emphasised the need to prioritise profitable client relationships and improve adviser productivity, including leveraging the bank’s newly approved national banking charter to expand banking services such as loans.

Despite these efforts, UBS shares have declined nearly 21 percent this year as investors await clarity on Swiss regulatory capital requirements and remain concerned about the U.S. wealth division’s performance. Analysts caution that a turnaround in U.S. asset flows is unlikely before the third quarter, signalling ongoing challenges for the bank’s largest economy operations.

Santander also released its fourth-quarter earnings a day early, which showed net profits of 3.76 billion euros ($4.45 billion) for the three-month period, ahead of consensus estimates of 3.41 billion euros, with the Spanish lender also unveiling a new 5-billion-euro share buyback program.

Novo Nordisk was down 4.9% after its share price plunged 18% in early dealmaking. The company released its results ahead of schedule Tuesday. It warned investors that it sees sales and profit growth declining this year, after it was hit by lower prices in the U.S. and the end of exclusivity for its blockbuster Wegovy and Ozempic weight loss drugs in China, Brazil, and Canada.
Earnings were in focus with Novartis, GSK, Infineon Technologies, Equinor, Credit Agricole, Handelsbanken, Carlsberg, and OMV all posting earnings reports on the day.

Shares in UBS were down 6.3% after Switzerland's largest lender reported a net profit of $1.2 billion in its fourth-quarter results, a 56% year-on-year rise which beat the $919 million forecast by analysts.

UBS profit beat overshadowed by worries over US wealth outflows
Private credit stocks plummet on concern about exposure to software industry disrupted by AI
sum: Shares of stocks with significant private credit market holdings were diving on fears about exposure to the industries being disrupted by artificial intelligence, most notably, software.
Shares of Blue Owl, TPG, Ares Management and KKR were all down by double digit percentages on Tuesday. Apollo Global was off by 7%. BlackRock shed 5%.

Publicly traded software stocks have been slammed this year as investors grew increasingly concerned about AI eating into their future growth and profit margins as companies use programs like Anthropic's Claude Code to build their own software. The iShares Software ETF is down 20% this year, including another 5% decline on Tuesday.

UBS analysts estimate 25% to 35% of the private-credit market is exposed to the risk of AI disruption (other sources say that software, specifically, accounts for about 20 percent of outstanding loans for private-direct lenders). By comparison, the high yield corporate bond market (Using the iShares iBoxx High Yield Corporate bond ETF as a proxy) has only 8 percent exposure to technology, reflecting a broader diversification among the syndicated market than the private-credit market.

The publicly traded alternative asset managers are impacted in two ways – their private-equity side could be hit because software is rerated lower, which may mean less carry for tech-exposed or tech-adjacent investments. And then on the private credit side, there's a risk of redemptions and, worst case, defaults. UBS estimates default rates could rise to 13% for private credit firms in the U.S. if AI triggers a big disruption. Comparatively, the default rate would be 4%for HY, UBS said.

"VC confidence in legacy enterprise SaaS business models has weakened materially over the last year with rapid change expected this year," stated the UBS research. "Rather than an 'AI Bust' scenario, we think an 'AI Disruption' scenario is more likely with differentiated risks at an individual subsector and credit level."

The "cockroaches" being talked about late last year (See JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon's comment) were specific situations, mostly alleged fraud. This software rerating is a big test for private credit because of sector concentration and the ubiquity of exposure.

items.t: UBS Set to Soar 41%? Bank of America Bets Big on Swiss Banking Shake-Up
sum: Bank of America analysts have projected a potentially sharp acceleration in earnings growth for UBS Group AG (NYSE:UBS), positioning the Swiss lender as the fastest sequential EPS grower among global banks. In a note led by Antonio Reale, the team estimated roughly 30% earnings-per-share growth between 2025 and 2028, prompting an upgrade to buy from neutral and a lift in the price target to the highest level among analysts tracked by Bloomberg. Reale noted that the equity story could be strengthened by a combination of proposed relief on Swiss capital requirements and continued momentum across wealth management and capital markets, particularly in Asia.
- Is UBS fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The analysts' more constructive stance follows recent developments in Switzerland, where legislators have proposed allowing UBS to use junior AT1 bonds rather than equity as capital backing for its foreign units. The shares rose as much as 3% on Tuesday, extending gains after last week's rally to a 17-year high. Reale suggested that a compromise on capital rules may be emerging, potentially reducing the need for additional CET1 capital to around $10.8 billion, compared with earlier scenarios that implied demands of up to $26 billion under stricter requirements.

Bank of America now views UBS as a top pick, with Reale lifting his price target to 48 Swiss francs, implying about 41% upside from Monday's close. He highlighted UBS's position as a regulatory outlier and said the proposed changes could mark a meaningful shift in its capital outlook, while also pointing to strength in Asian wealth management, capital markets activity in the region, and ongoing cost-reduction efforts. Taken together, these factors could support a more favorable earnings trajectory over the coming years, should the regulatory backdrop evolve along the lines currently being discussed.
